vocab.definition: a Group 1 metal with one outer electron.
alkaline solution formed when Group 1 reacts with water.
Group 1 atoms lose 1 electron to form a 1+ ion.

misconceptions.wrong: Alkali metals are hard and dense.
misconceptions.right: They are soft and have low density.
They lose one electron to form 1+ ions.

questions.text: State the number of electrons in the outer shell of a Group 1 atom. [1 mark]
Name the two products when sodium reacts with water. [2 marks]
Explain why reactivity increases down Group 1. [3 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Think about the distance of the outer electron from the nucleus.

questions.text: Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A Group 1 atom ______ one electron. Reactivity ______ down the group.

questions.text: Predict how potassium reacts with water compared with lithium. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Bigger atom → outer electron is further out → lost more easily → more reactive.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does the resulting solution turn universal indicator purple?
